messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT P1 — multiple prod deploys failing due to GitHub Actions / Packages errors. Alerting on-call. Error: 502/500 when pushing artifacts to GitHub Packages and 429/503 for API calls. Lambda deploys blocked. 
Maya Patel: ack — I'm on it. Paging Samir for CI/workflow triage. 
Samir Gupta: I'm looking. Re-runs fail immediately with `error: failed to upload to registry: 502 Bad Gateway` from `docker/build-push-action@v4`. Also seeing `GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit 503` in logs. 
Leah Chen: Confirmed. Builds that rely on GitHub Packages can't publish, so downstream deploy job times out waiting for image/artifact. Canary deploys are stuck. 
Tomas Garcia: Scope — is this only GitHub Packages / Actions, or also GitHub auth API? I saw OAuth token exchanges returning 500 earlier. Could be a broader API outage on GitHub side. 
Samir Gupta: Looks like a combination: package registry endpoints 502/503, API returning 5xx for some endpoints. I'm opening a ticket with GitHub Support (ticket #GH-112798) and posting to https://www.githubstatus.com/ — they're showing degraded performance on Actions and Packages. 
Maya Patel: Customer impact: customers on recent hotfix channel can't get patch deployed; some customer-facing bugs remain open. Escalate to CS for customer comms. 
Priya Nair: Notified CS. Recommend a short status banner: "We're investigating GitHub Actions/Packages issues affecting deploys; teams may see failed builds or delayed hotfixes." I'll post to status.redwood.com once we have mitigation plan. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
Leah Chen: Mitigation options I can apply quickly: 1) Build artifacts on an internal runner and upload artifacts to S3, update deploy job to pull from S3. 2) Bypass publish step and use prebuilt images from last successful commit (if acceptable). 3) Run a self-hosted runner in our infra to try to push to a different registry (ECR/GCR). 
Tomas Garcia: Option 1 is fastest. I can spin up a temp runner cluster and a one-off Job to build the hotfix and push to our private registry (ECR). Steps: 
```
# on infra runner
git checkout hotfix/2026-03-15
./ci/build.sh && docker tag app:hotfix <aws_account>.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/app:hotfix-<sha>
aws ecr get-login-password | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin <aws_account>.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
docker push <aws_account>.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/app:hotfix-<sha>
aws s3 cp dist/* s3://redwood-temp-artifacts/hotfix-<sha>/ --acl private
```
I'll coordinate with Leah to change the deploy job to use `DEPLOY_ARTIFACT_URL` pointing at S3/ECR. 
Samir Gupta: Note: changing deploy pipeline to pull from S3/ECR requires patch to our manifests and a bypass of the GH Actions publish step. We should gate this behind a one-off approval. Also check SBOM/signature requirements for images — security may need to sign-off on bypassing standard signing flow. 
Maya Patel: Security is paged. @security oncall — we may need to temporarily accept unsigned artifact for emergency hotfix; will track audit log. 
SRE Rotation Bot: Handoff scheduled — Maya handing to Tomas at 1769900200 UTC for remediation until secondary is available. 
Tomas Garcia: I'm taking ownership of mitigations. Leah, can you prepare the pipeline patch? I'll test the runner build now. 
Leah Chen: Pushing a small patch to `ci/pipeline-hotfix-s3.yml` that skips `publish_to_github` step and sets `ARTIFACT_URL` to S3. Patch ready in PR: `github.com/redwood/infra/pull/8242` (won't merge to main; will be applied as patch to deploy job). 
Samir Gupta: Quick check — deploy console shows queued canary at 40% that requires artifacts. If we can get ECR image pushed and manifest updated, we can advance canary manually. 
Priya Nair: Approving emergency pipeline tweak for hotfix only. CS: prepare customer comms with ETA ~60–90m initially, will update. 
Maya Patel: Operational notes: 1) don't remove rollback guards; 2) increase monitoring on canary metrics; 3) record all manual steps in incident doc. 
Leah Chen: Patch applied to canary pipeline. Initiating self-hosted build now. If build and push succeed, I'll trigger manual deploy to canary. 
Samir Gupta: Github support updated: they acknowledged degraded performance and are investigating. No ETA yet. Ticket GH-112798 updated. 
Tomas Garcia: Build succeeded on self-hosted runner. Pushed image to ECR and uploaded artifacts to S3. Manually updated manifest to point `image: <aws_account>.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/app:hotfix-<sha>` and triggered canary deploy. 
Maya Patel: Canary started. Monitoring logs. :eyes: 
Leah Chen: Canary passed basic health checks at 5m — metrics look stable. Proceeding to advance to 100% per runbook manual-deploy steps. 
Priya Nair: Notifying customers in the next 10m that we're deploying a hotfix via alternate pipeline; action required: none from customers. Will include link to incident thread and status page. 
Maya Patel: After full rollout, we should revert pipeline patch and re-run standard CI once GitHub is healthy. Also add a follow-up to runbook: include ECR/S3 fallback steps and approval checklist. 
Samir Gupta: Post-incident actions: 1) add automated failover to our publish step to attempt ECR on `github packages` failures; 2) test self-hosted runner readiness quarterly; 3) incident writeup. 
SRE Rotation Bot: Incident acknowledged closed once postmortem PR is created. 
Maya Patel: Closing notes: Hotfix deployed via ECR/S3 fallback at 1769900465. No customer data exposed. Logging and audit entries recorded. Will keep GH ticket open until GitHub resolves. Thanks team. :tada:
